scope.live_owned_paths_cleanup: Both live runs confirmed three guarded absences; fresh native loopback also confirmed three guarded absences.

rulings_in_order: Engine byte/token admission limits apply to actual three-way merging; equal/one-sided fast paths may bypass the engine within existing protocol limits — otherwise a large one-sided local edit would wrongly become server-wins fallback — if wrong, large fast-path source copies could cost memory/latency, so retain bounded existing protocol limits and test the path.

Task 3 may add save_local_from_base_outcome while retaining the existing save_local_from_base wrapper until Task 5 migrates callers to LocalSaveOutcome — intermediate tasks must compile without prematurely implementing editor behavior — if wrong, a temporary wrapper increases API surface and must be removed once all callers migrate.

Recovery job state changes (acknowledgement, unknown marking, relocation and readback completion) must carry the expected OperationId as well as event/ordinal — event/ordinal survives relocation, so an old attempt must never complete a newer destination's job — if wrong, this adds parameters and attempt-history checks but does not change product behavior. Claim may return the current operation atomically; subsequent mutations must use that captured identity.

Use one retained SQLite monotonic generation clock for page source and recovery-draft generations, assigning fresh values on insert and relevant source updates — per-row defaults/counters permit ABA after same-path deletion/recreation, including an identical reinserted draft — if wrong, the extra counter write adds latency; measure within the existing single-owner transaction and keep position/recency changes excluded. Existing migrated rows may start0 because no old runtime token survives migration. Checked i64 exhaustion must fail safely.

Persist a typed automatic-recovery cause (Overlap, NoCommonBase, BudgetFallback, AuthoredDraft) as event metadata, outside the observation fingerprint — the spec requires a local reason and equal observations must reuse identity even if resource availability changes — if wrong, the extra enum may require extension for a newly supported cause; source remains unchanged and no current runtime rows are deployed.

Execute the already-approved floating-chrome implementation after Task5 and before Task6 final acceptance/whole-branch review — one final review must cover both original user requests, and running it before UI would require redundant broad validation — if wrong, a UI regression may delay the combined acceptance boundary; sync task reviews still remain ordered and separate. This refines the earlier 'after sync' scheduling note, without changing feature scope.

Task4 may add a new additive migration and narrowly scoped retired-delete watch store module plus explicit-trash hook — existing outbox states and page-cascade lifetime cannot encode retired destructive evidence and independent repair authority safely — if wrong, this adds persistence/API surface; keep ordinary create-only repair on the existing outbox and do not generalize recovery upload jobs. Preserve immutable evidence across restart; later explicit user trash must atomically supersede old repair authority. See unknown-delete-watch-audit.md.

A retired DELETE watch is passive safety monitoring, distinct from an outstanding write; report content sync against the latest acknowledged/read-back canonical/recovery obligations, while retaining the unresolved old-request evidence — no finite readback can prove old HTTP terminality, and treating a permanently unknowable retired request as an active write would strand status forever — if wrong, content may transiently disappear before a delayed-delete watch repairs it. Never claim request cancellation/terminality, and any materialized, denied or unknown repair remains pending/failed and durable. No silent expiry of watch authority; explicit later user deletion can supersede it.

True clean two-sided merges also retain base/local/remote/chosen in local kept history, without creating synced recovery uploads — Task3's preservation wording is unqualified and automatic source replacement should be reversible; identity/one-sided fast paths retain existing behavior — if wrong, retained snapshots increase local storage use. Repeated unchanged observations must not duplicate them.

After recovery destination relocation, retired create-only attempts are passive readback watches; only the current immutable first-create attempt fences ordinary destination edits, and exact acknowledgement of the current copy settles that event/ordinal's preservation obligation — old HTTP terminality can be permanently unknowable, but the required source is durably preserved by the acknowledged replacement, and create-only late work cannot overwrite an occupied edited page — if wrong, a delayed old attempt may still create an extra recovery page at an emptied old destination. Retain immutable attempt history/discovery and never claim its request terminality; current blocked/unknown jobs and any real pending writes remain pending. Task4 must update Task2's conservative all-attempt status/fence queries and test post-relocation edits and replacement acknowledgement with old watch retained.

Distinguish definitive guard-rejected DELETE responses from transport-uncertain DELETEs with persisted finite terminal evidence before readback/restart — a rejected request cannot execute later, so granting it indefinite resurrection authority would undo legitimate future external deletions — if wrong, the extra evidence transition/schema field adds complexity; keep it narrow and do not classify transport/proxy5xx failures as terminal. Both paths preserve/reconcile edits without retrying old destructive intent; only genuinely uncertain delayed work authorizes repair.

Task5 may add a narrow typed editor-rebase preparation/checked commit and typed recovery provenance, preserving displayed baseline B, original input U, durable canonical S and genuine HTTP base H separately — Task3's HTTP-shaped remote is installed as server base, so fabricating it from dirty canonical S corrupts validator/source meaning; stale-save-only can omit independent pending S edits — if wrong, the extra API/metadata increases integration cost. Reuse existing merge executor, history, immutable upload and CAS helpers; no second merge engine, fabricated authored revision, false HTTP observation, or non-atomic recovery registration. See editor-rebase-store-audit.md.

Task5 may add focused migration007 and a durable editor-handoff journal/module — ordinary stale saves must acknowledge exact U before merge/draft gates, while retaining canonical S and B/H evidence so restart can merge S-only pending changes — if wrong, extra replay/coalescing state increases complexity. Keep pending handoff unsynced, restore latest accepted U to the editor before replay even offline/unknown, retain genuine H separately, and preserve branch baseline/displacedS across subsequent U2 saves. New user trash/restore must invalidate stale installation; reuse existing checked merge/preservation pipeline.

Permit a fixture-only local pointer-event filter scoped to the owned generated NSWindow, distinguishing tagged synthetic events and passing all other windows/non-pointer events — traced real pointer moves from the active desktop repeatedly canceled scripted hover while key stayed true; requiring mouse inactivity would interrupt the user — if wrong, fixture filtering may hide interactions with physical input, so leave physical gestures as manual gates and keep product ChromeMonitor unchanged with scoped cleanup.

Permit a cfg(test)-only pub(crate) StoreHandle getter returning its actual shared MergeExecutor clone for the existing private stalled-merge unit test — separate executors only establish CPU/storage coexistence, not the real store-slot fallback/preservation boundary — if wrong, the extra test seam couples the unit test to store construction; keep it absent from production/public API, use existing private finite merge_with stall, and do not claim native typing/frame latency from storage acknowledgements.

Retain the unattributed Slint static/palette convergence diagnostic as an explicit minor investigation, with no suppression or speculative product correction — accepted floating/native routes and captures show no demonstrated failure and equivalent baseline attribution is unavailable — if wrong, an initialization/layout performance defect may remain undetected until focused baseline/change-tracker investigation.

Accept the final review's semantic-prose limit: automatic policy guarantees deterministic selection and exact preservation, not inferred author intent — contradictory meaning has no verifiable universal resolution — if wrong, chosen prose may require manual review of the preserved alternative.

Keep physical IME/VoiceOver/directional-selection/gestures/Spaces/older-hardware checks as open release gates — source review and synthetic owned input do not establish those capabilities — if wrong, physical/native fidelity defects remain undiscovered before release testing.

Keep native frame/typing latency under a deliberately stalled shared executor unverified, separately from measured SQLite acknowledgements — storage timings do not demonstrate frame/input behavior — if wrong, a CPU-stall interaction could remain unmeasured despite durable-save progress.

Label deployed acceptance as controlled exact-path relay evidence, with direct unrelayed native routing unverified — this was required to exclude unrelated page bodies and the normal app store — if wrong, a direct-routing-specific integration failure remains untested.

Build only the authorized ad-hoc development bundle after clean review; leave Developer ID/notarization/clean-install/upgrade/distribution gates open — no signing identity, upload, app replacement or real Keychain use was authorized — if wrong, development verification will not predict distribution/upgrade behavior.

Treat license/advisory checks as dated generated evidence rather than new legal or vulnerability certification — unchanged lock SHA reuses the approved audit and verified license texts — if wrong, later/unlisted advisories or attribution defects require a new audit.

Extend the final correction with the narrowly required denied-GET readback backoff fix and scoped recheck — fresh re-review proved a new load-bearing hot loop introduced by permission readmission, and the higher-priority instruction to complete authorized work forbids packaging a known broken path merely to satisfy the skill's one-wave stop rule — if wrong, this adds implementation/verification time and another focused review; preserve all original addressed verdicts and limit changes to the new GET-403 edge.
